title: ‘I am very concerned’: Bill Gates says the world needs a plan to deal with AI, and he has three ideas to start
description: Bill Gates says the "turbulent AI era" has arrived, and the AI industry is crossing safety lines it once promised to respect. In a new essay and an interview with GeekWire, he lays out three ideas for managing what's coming: new national and global institutions, a category of jobs reserved for humans, and a tax on AI and robots. title: AI agent platform Ringg raises $10 million in Series A extension led by Peak XV Partners
description: Bengaluru-based AI startup Ringg AI has raised $10 million in an extension of its Series A funding round, led by Peak XV Partners , with existing investors Arkam Ventures and Capital 2B also participating. The startup had previously raised $5.5 million in Series A funding earlier this year, taking the total size of the round to $15.5 million. Ringg, founded by Siddharth Tripathi, Utkarsh Shukla and Kali Charan Vemuru, develops AI agents for businesses and processes about 20 million call attempts each month. Its customers include Flipkart, Practo, Groww and PolicyBazaar. The startup began as a text-to-speech company called DesiVocal before shifting towards enterprise AI agents after finding the cost of developing its own speech models difficult to sustain. Ringg initially focused on high-volume tasks including outbound calling, lead qualification and loan collection, but has since moved towards more complex business processes. “At the start, we were doing high-volume, low-complexity use cases like outbound calling, lead qualification, loan collection, and more,” Tripathi said. “We quickly realized these are not sticky use cases, and so it’s always going to be a price game,” he added. The startup is now targeting applications including healthcare appointment booking, e-commerce cart recovery, and customer onboarding and know-your-customer checks for financial services businesses. Its voice agent is deployed across 1,200 clinics on healthcare platform Practo, where it helps patients book appointments and follow up after visits. Voice calls account for more than 70% of Ringg’s business, but the startup is expanding into chat, WhatsApp and browser-based automation as it looks to offer a broader range of enterprise AI services. “We are trying to position ourselves as a platform for agents that bring outcomes or get things done rather than voice agents for enterprises,” Tripathi said. Most of Ringg’s customers are based in India, with a smaller presence in the Middle East and the US. It plans to use Global Capability Centres in India as part of its international expansion strategy, offering automation alongside human support operations used by multinational companies. Ringg develops some of its own speech recognition and speech generation models, while its platform can also direct tasks to different models depending on the requirements of a particular workflow. The startup eventually wants to control more of the voice technology stack, including infrastructure and deployment, although the cost of doing so remains a constraint. Rishen Kapoor, a principal at Peak XV Partners, said Ringg’s technical background had helped it tackle more complex enterprise workflows. “Because of the technical capabilities, they can actually do these hard-won enterprise workflows end to end. They can complete these higher-value tasks like merchant onboarding, like L1 and L2 support, with quality and with consistency,” Kapoor said. Ringg has 40 employees, with more than 15 joining in the past three months. The startup is hiring engineers to work closely with enterprise customers on deployments, as well as researchers focused on reducing the cost of running its AI models.
